strategy_title: Doubling BLOCK_K Doubles Shared Memory, Kills Occupancy
strategy_description: Increasing BLOCK_K from 32 to 64 in a Triton GEMM kernel doubled the dynamic shared memory per block from ~65 KB to ~131 KB, which reduced Block Limit Shared Mem from 3 to 1 block per SM. This halved theoretical occupancy from 12.5% to 6.25% and caused Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction to jump from 4.76 to 12.33, indicating severe latency-hiding loss. The net effect was a 6.3x slowdown despite the intent to reduce loop iterations, because the occupancy collapse far outweighed any loop-overhead savings. When a kernel is already register-bound (255 registers/thread, Block Limit Registers=2), any change that further reduces Block Limit Shared Mem below the register-imposed limit will cause catastrophic occupancy regression.
slow_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_K = 32 -> dynamic_smem = 65 KB -> Block Limit Shared Mem = 3
for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K=32):
    a = tl.load(A_ptr + k_offsets)  # shape [BLOCK_M, 32]
    b = tl.load(B_ptr + k_offsets)  # shape [32, BLOCK_N]
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_K = 64 -> dynamic_smem = 131 KB -> Block Limit Shared Mem = 1 (REGRESSION)
for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K=64):
    a = tl.load(A_ptr + k_offsets)  # shape [BLOCK_M, 64]
    b = tl.load(B_ptr + k_offsets)  # shape [64, BLOCK_N]
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)  # ALLOW_TF32 was NOT changed in actual diff
applicable_when: Never applicable when the kernel is already at the shared-memory occupancy limit (Block Limit Shared Mem <= Block Limit Registers). Increasing tile size in this regime always reduces occupancy further.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel has Block Limit Shared Mem <= Block Limit Registers (shared memory is already the binding occupancy constraint, or tied with registers). In this case, any increase to BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, or BLOCK_K that grows shared memory allocation will reduce occupancy and increase latency stalls. Also: the actual diff did NOT change ALLOW_TF32 (it remained False), so TF32 Tensor Cores were never actually enabled — the plan was partially mis-implemented.
framework_notes: In Triton, dynamic shared memory per block scales as (BLOCK_M * BLOCK_K + BLOCK_K * BLOCK_N) * dtype_bytes for double-buffered tiles. Doubling BLOCK_K doubles this allocation. Always check Block Limit Shared Mem vs Block Limit Registers before increasing tile dimensions. The diff also shows ALLOW_TF32 was NOT changed from False to True in the actual kernel code (only USE_FAST_ACCUM changed), meaning the TF32 strategy was never actually tested — the regression is purely from the BLOCK_K increase.
